name: After § 10
title: INTERIM REPORT on the proposal for a Council regulation laying down the Multiannual Financial Framework for the years 2028 to 2034
part_text: 10a. Objects to an approach that involves increasing flexibility in the allocation of resources within the Union’s programmes, and stresses that, far from being an appropriate structural response, increased recourse to margins and special instruments has helped to weaken budget predictability, transparency over financial decisions and oversight; notes that, as found by the European Court of Auditors in its special report 18/2025, the Commission failed to carry out an ex ante or retrospective evaluation of the functioning of the main flexibility tools, in particular the margins, the Single Margin Instrument and the Flexibility Instrument, making it impossible to gauge their real effectiveness or to draw lessons from them for the future; underscores that this failure to carry out evaluations runs counter to the principles of effective risk management and evidence-based policymaking; reiterates that any decisions relating to the allocation of funding to specific policy objectives must be adopted in their entirety by the competent budgetary authority based on the EU Treaties; deplores the fact that the indicative nomenclature proposed in the programme legislation remains insufficient and leads to a lack of clarity over budgetary priorities; objects to the introduction or strengthening of additional special instruments in the post-2027 MFF, since this would risk increasing the fragmentation, complexity and opaqueness of the Union’s budgetary framework;
